footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net loss: includes a $2.4M income tax benefit. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 14.7% to $104M in 2025. Net interest income rose 18.1% to $86.5M and noninterest income was flat at $17.0M; noninterest expense rose 20.1%, and the provision for credit losses was $21.7M, versus $2.1M.
Net loss was −$3.3M, versus $11.5M, or −$0.18 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 84.8% versus 81.0%.
sources: Avidia Bancorp, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
